newsitem.title: UK: Conservatives may still extend UK VAT - Labour.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives may still extend UK VAT - Labour.

text.p: Gordon Brown, British opposition Labour party's finance spokesman, said on Wednesday that Conservative candidates were being advised by their bosses not to rule out extending VAT.
"In Conservative central office briefings, Conservative candidates are being specifically advised not to rule out extending VAT," Brown said at a news conference.

He said a Conservative briefing paper said if asked whether VAT could be extended to children's clothes, books and newspapers, candidates should answer: "The Chancellor has quite rightly refused to give this commitment".
Labour has promised not to extended VAT to children's clothes, food, books, newspapers and public transport.It pledges to reduce VAT on heating fuel to five percent from eight percent at present.

"The question for (Prime Minister) John Major and (Chancellor of the Exchequer) Kenneth Clarke is why will they not match Labour's commitment?" he said. "And why will they not cut VAT on fuel to five percent?"
